question: In 2025, Shubhanshu Shukla conducted an International Space Station (ISS) experiment with moong and methi seeds to study:

options.text: Soil nutrient cycling under space conditions
Resistance of legumes to common pesticides

solution:
The correct answer is __**Seed germination under microgravity conditions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seed germination under microgravity conditions** was the focus of Shubhanshu Shukla's experiment in 2025 on the International Space Station (ISS).
 
• The study aimed to understand how seeds like **moong** (green gram) and **methi** (fenugreek) germinate in the absence of Earth's gravity.
 
• Microgravity poses unique challenges for biological processes such as seed germination, including issues like **water distribution, nutrient absorption, and root growth orientation**.
 
• Understanding seed behavior in space is critical for the development of **space farming**, a necessary step for long-term human space exploration and colonization.
 
• This experiment contributes to the field of astrobiology and sheds light on the viability of growing food in extraterrestrial environments. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Microgravity and Its Effects:**

 
 
• Microgravity is a condition where objects appear to be weightless and experience minimal gravitational force. It is common in space.
 
• Under microgravity, water tends to form spherical droplets, and nutrient distribution becomes uneven, which can complicate plant growth.
 
 
 
• **Space Farming:**
 
 
• Space farming involves growing crops in extraterrestrial environments, such as the ISS or other planets like Mars.
 
• It is essential for providing a sustainable source of food for astronauts on long-duration missions.
 
• Plants also contribute to life support systems by producing oxygen and removing carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Moong and Methi Seeds:**
 
 
• **Moong** (green gram) is a protein-rich legume widely used in Indian cuisine.
 
• **Methi** (fenugreek) is known for its nutritional and medicinal properties, including its ability to reduce blood sugar levels.
 
• Both are fast-growing plants, making them ideal for short-term experiments like those conducted on the ISS.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Seed Germination Studies in Space:**
 
 
• Understanding seed germination in space helps scientists design systems for growing crops in extraterrestrial environments.
 
• It also contributes to our understanding of how plants adapt to extreme conditions, which can have applications on Earth, such as in arid or nutrient-poor soils.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges in Space Farming:**

 
 
• Watering plants in microgravity is difficult as water does not flow naturally but instead forms floating droplets.
 
• Lack of soil in space requires innovative techniques like hydroponics or aeroponics for plant growth.
 
• Light exposure in spacecraft is artificial, requiring the use of LED systems to simulate sunlight.
 
 
 
• **Previous Experiments:**
 
 
• NASA has conducted experiments on growing crops like lettuce, radishes, and wheat aboard the ISS.
 
• The European Space Agency (ESA) has also studied plant growth under simulated Martian and lunar conditions.
 
 
 
• **Future Implications:**
 
 
• Successful space farming can reduce the dependency on Earth for food supplies during space missions.
 
• It can also pave the way for establishing self-sustaining human colonies on planets like Mars.
